title: Consistency sentinel for KV prefetch and config rollouts
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: Implement a lightweight, reproducible 'consistency sentinel' harness that catches semantic regressions caused specifically by KV/prefix cache hits and prefetch behavior during model/config rollouts. Motivation: We continue to see low-frequency but high-impact cases where cache hits (especially prefetching of KV entries) change generated outputs for a subset of prompts. Existing audits focus on overall output drift but do not isolate prefetch-induced divergences or correlate them to rollout config changes (kernel selection, kv-eviction heuristics, prefetch window). Goal: provide an automated, fast experiment suite used in CI and canary to detect changes in output semantics attributable to cache hit state, with clear gating thresholds for rollouts.
background: Observed problems: production incident on 2026-02-18 where a dedicated customer reported hallucination regressions after a runtime patch that altered KV prefetch ordering. Manually replaying requests showed divergence only when the KV proxy returned warm cached entries. Existing datasets (golden-response sets) catch many regressions but are noisy when comparing warmed vs cold-paths because of nondeterministic tokenization and async prefetch timing. We need a reproducible harness that: (1) forces deterministic KV hit/miss scenarios, (2) attributes delta to cache state vs model/config change, and (3) produces a compact signature for quick triage and alerting.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible binary test harness (consistency-sentinel) that can run in CI and on canary clusters and produce per-prompt diff summaries for warm vs cold KV states.
The harness must support toggles: force_kv_hit, force_kv_miss, prefetch_on/off, and simulated_eviction, exposed as test params.
A scoring function that classifies regressions into: semantic_break (high), formatting_shift (medium), whitespace/tokenization_noise (low) with thresholds configurable via runtime-2.3 rollout config.
Alerting rules and a dashboard with run-level SLOs: >0.5% semantic_break on canary triggers rollback or manual approval; >1% in prod flags incident investigation.
Documentation and runbook linked in attachments and a reference GitHub PR that implements the harness.
CI gate: any change touching kv-prefetch, kernel-selection, or cache-eviction code must pass sentinel with no semantic_breaks on the canonical prompt set for 5 consecutive runs.
Synthetic signature generation: produce a 64-byte base64 signature per-run that captures token-aligned diff stats to speed triage and reduce storage.
Integration tests that exercise warm-paths using recorded KV snapshots and deterministic model seeds to eliminate nondeterminism in evaluation runs.
test_plan: Create canonical prompt set (500 prompts) drawn from production traffic strata (short/long/context-switching/structured-output), with labeled golden outputs.
Implement harness to replay prompts with: (A) cold KV (fresh node), (B) warm KV (preloaded snapshot), (C) prefetch_on vs prefetch_off matrix.
Use deterministic RNG seed and fixed tokenizer version to remove source of nondeterminism.
Compute token-aligned diffs and semantic similarity (embedding cosine with threshold 0.88) and detect cases where semantic similarity drops but length and log-prob stable.
Run ablation experiments for eviction policy, prefetch window size, and kernel selection to map parameter sensitivity surface.
Produce nightly sentinel runs against mainline and track 30-day rolling windows for alerting baselines.
Add sentinel to canary pipeline: run on 10% of canary traffic and block rollout if semantic_break > 0.5% across canonical set.
Validate with manual inspection and pair-programming session with model-onboarding team for first three rollouts.
Measure false positive rate by comparing sentinel findings against human-labeled regressions from previous incidents.
Create automated PR check that links to the sentinel run summary and signature as a comment on the PR touching cache-related files.
If gating fails, automatically annotate impacted prompts and link to a deterministically reproducible HTML diff artifact for debugging.
Establish retention policy for sentinel artifacts: signatures kept indefinitely; full diffs for 90 days.
Run load-smoke to ensure harness scales to 1000 parallel prompt replays without affecting canary SLA.
out_of_scope: Full-scale production A/B testing of cache policies (this ticket focuses on detection and gating, not policy optimization).
Changes to model training or tokenizer updates (these are separate projects but we will surface tokenizer mismatches).
Building a generic semantic-regression detector for all subsystems; scope limited to cache-prefetch and warmed KV semantics.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: High false positives due to tokenization changes. Mitigation: lock tokenizer version for sentinel runs and report tokenizer mismatch as separate label.
Risk: Sentinel adds latency to canary rollout. Mitigation: run sentinel on sampled traffic and run deterministic replay in parallel to avoid slow path in production.
Risk: Snapshotting KV state may leak PII. Mitigation: use synthetic or scrubbed snapshots and enforce KMS access controls for artifacts.

Risk: Embedding-based semantic scoring can miss format-sensitive regressions. Mitigation: composite score that includes n-gram overlap and structure-aware checks (JSON schema validation where applicable).
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed — built prototype that can force_kv_hit by replaying requests into a mocked kv-proxy with preloaded entries. Results: found 17 candidate prompts with divergences in warm vs cold runs on the runtime-2.2 branch.

2026-03-04: Design review with PM (Leah Kim) and SRE (Jonah Reed). Decided to represent results as compact base64 signature plus human-readable diff; approved alert thresholds for canary (0.5%) and prod (1%).
2026-03-06: Implemented token-aligned diff exporter and uploaded HTML diffs to the artifacts bucket (gs://redwood-sentinel/artifacts/ENG-61234/). Example artifact linked in attachments.
2026-03-08: UX review with Console team — agreed to add a sentinel card to model rollout page showing signature, top failing prompts, and quick links to diffs.
2026-03-10: Security review kickoff — flagged KV snapshot scrubbing, draft policy created (see attachments) and awaiting security approval (ticket SEC-2981).
decisions: Use deterministic replay with fixed seeds rather than recording live production traffic to avoid nondeterminism.
Composite scoring: embedding similarity + token-aligned diff ratios + schema checks for structured responses.
Expose sentinel toggles as config flags in rollout manifest so product teams can opt-in for higher-sensitivity checks during risky rollouts.
Keep signatures small and indexed so triage can match failing runs across environments quickly without fetching full diffs.
Prefetch behavior will be tested as a matrix (on/off) and as a window-size sweep to identify sensitive ranges.
Gate: block rollouts automatically on semantic_break > configured threshold for canary; require manual override with documented remediation steps.
attachments: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2B_example_kv_snapshots -- scrubbed KV snapshots used for replay
next_steps: Finish PR feedback loop and merge initial harness to mainline (blocking: unit test flakiness on macOS runner).
Add sentinel to canary pipeline and run for two rollouts to calibrate false positive rate.
Work with Console team to add sentinel card and alerting knobs (UX tasks created).
Complete security review and enforce snapshot scrub pipeline before retention storage.
Prepare a post-mortem template for any sentinel-triggered rollback events to iterate on thresholds and datasets.
